Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: split invoice cycle / payment cadence flexibility

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Sundial is excited about Redwood’s latency and cost controls for our inference workloads. Procurement asked me to reach out about payment cadence. We’re moving to a centralized AP process and need invoices aligned with our quarterly budgeting cycle.

Specifically we’d like to propose the following for the initial annual contract: 1) 30% upfront at PO acceptance, 2) then invoicing on a quarterly cadence (three invoices after the initial payment) with Net-60 payment terms on each invoice. Alternatively, if Redwood prefers a smaller number of invoices, we can accept Net-90 on quarterly invoices.

Attached is our PO (Sundial_PO_6543.pdf) and a short worksheet showing our cashflow timing. Can Redwood approve the split-cycle / Net-60/Net-90 exception for this account? This is a strategic deployment (clinical inference) for us and we expect to scale seats in Q1 next year.

Appreciate quick confirmation so Procurement can move forward with signatures.

Best,
Alicia Torres
Head of Procurement, Sundial Health

Hi Alicia — thanks for the PO and the worksheet. I’ve looped in Ben (Sales) and Lauren (RevOps) to confirm impact and approvals.

High level: Redwood is open to customer-specific cadence for strategic deals but we need an internal approval for Net-60/Net-90 exceptions and any staged invoicing. Can you confirm the proposed payment schedule (dates or triggers) you expect for the four payments, and whether acceptance is milestone- or date-driven? That will help finance model AR and confirm whether we need a partial prepayment (we typically ask 20–30% upfront for quarterly-split deals).

I’ll follow up with an internal note to expedite review.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Ben — quick finance/ops input. I pulled comparable cases: we approved quarterly invoicing + Net-60 on two recent strategic accounts but required 25–30% upfront and a clause that ties invoicing to delivery acceptance. Impacts:
- DSO increase estimated +18 days on average; cashflow hit can be mitigated with the deposit.
- We should also add a clause: invoices not paid within 30 days of due date revert to standard monthly billing and suspend future deliveries until cured. Works in our favor for escalation.

Policy ask to leadership: this is within the margin buffer for strategic accounts, but anything beyond Net-90 or >120 days DSO needs VP Sales sign-off.

Lauren
Head of Revenue Operations

Rachel / Ben / Lauren — I reviewed the PO and the revenue ops note. Given Sundial is strategic (clinical deployment) and expected to expand in Q1, I approve the conditional exception:

- Terms: 30% deposit at SOW/PO acceptance (Invoice 1).
- Three subsequent invoices issued on a quarterly cadence for the remaining balance. Each of those invoices will be Net-60.
- If Sundial requests Net-90 on any invoice, limit approval to a single invoice and require CFO-level signoff from Redwood.
- Add contract language: payment triggers tied to delivery acceptance; late payment reversion clause (suspend services / revert to standard monthly terms).

Next steps for Rachel: send Alicia the updated SOW with the 30% deposit and quarterly invoicing language, capture DocuSign and procurement contact, and copy Legal for a quick redline. Also confirm whether Andrew (Redwood Finance) should send an AR holdback notice template.

I authorize this on a conditional basis — if legal flags revenue recognition issues we’ll revisit.
